newsitem.title: USA: Starr wins longer term for Whitewater grand jury.
newsitem.headline: Starr wins longer term for Whitewater grand jury.

text.p: Whitewater prosecutors succeeded on Tuesday in extending the life of a grand jury studying the political and business affairs of President Bill Clinton and his wife Hillary.

U.S. District Judge Susan Webber Wright granted a request by Whitewater special prosecutor Kenneth Starr to give the grand jury an extra six months to continue the probe. The grand jury's dismissal had been scheduled for May 7 but it will now work until Nov. 7.

"The United States submits, and the Court finds, that an extension of the grand jury is in the public interest ... in order for the grand jury to conclude its investigation of matters pending before it," Wright said in a ruling.
Starr filed a motion earlier on Tuesday saying the grand jury had gathered substantial evidence of obstruction of justice and needed more time to pursue its probe.
"This grand jury has heard extensive evidence of possible obstruction of justice relating to matters within the Independent Counsel's jurisdiction," he said.
Starr is investigating whether the president or first lady Hillary Rodham Clinton played any part in fraudulent business deals in Arkansas in the mid-1980s, when Clinton was state governor.
